title: Real Research Today: Early-Detection Nanosensors
definition: Today's documented research behind Early-Detection Nanosensors.
description:
The road to Early-Detection Nanosensors is already being paved. The WHO's ICD-11 added an extension code for aging-related conditions, legitimizing the field. CRISPR-based therapies (Casgevy) won the first regulatory approvals for sickle cell disease in 2023.

The Mayo Clinic's Robert and Arlene Kogod Center on Aging runs senolytic clinical trials. Together these programs form the blood monitors foundation that Early-Detection Nanosensors will build on — the sensor logistics results, the signal algorithms methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as sensor logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: Early-Detection Nanosensors Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Early-Detection Nanosensors: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Early-Detection Nanosensors — nanosensors finding disease years before symptoms.

Phase 1 — Prove (blood monitors): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (sensor logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (signal algorithms): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (implant safety): sensor hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and diagnostics-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
